findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
findings.comment: There were two drinks stored directly above clean dishes on a storage rack inside of the dish room. Shown to the PIC and the drinks were placed in a designated drink area. Ensure that personal drinks are never stored above clean dishes to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11(A) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, an EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of TOBACCO PRODUCTS only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; or other items needing protection can not result.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Grease droplets formed within the duct work of the hood system were observed dripping onto the flat top grill. The hood baffles were removed to be cleaned, however, the ansul and duct work were heavily accumulation with grease debris. The last visit from the facility’s technical company, Cintas, visited the facility last on January 14, 2026. Discussed the need to have the hood serviced more often. Will follow up on August 10, 2026 to see that system has been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Despite the facility being in full operation, there wasn’t a sanitizer solution present in the bar area. The bar area serves drinks, handles garnishes, and also slices fruits, therefore, a sanitizer solution is needed during operating hours. Ensure that a sanitizer solution is present to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting properly sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas are in need of cleaning:
- ice buildup was observed on the floor of the walk in unit (directly under air compressor)
- both bottom selves of the drawer coolers along tho cook-line were observed with accumulated debris, one drawer stores spring mix lettuce and the other drawer stores meats
- floor underneath produce wash station was observed with accumulated food deris
When time permits, be sure to clean the areas referenced above to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was a carton of eggs stored above ready-to-eat (RTE) foods in a small cooler along the cookline. Shown to the PIC and the eggs were discarded to correct the violation. The PIC mentioned that the raw eggs belonged to an employee. Be sure to educate employees on separating personal foods from food intended for public consumption. Also, ensure that raw animal protein is never stored above RTE foods to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed a bottle of degreaser stored on top of the veggie wash station where produce is sliced. Shown to the person-in-charge and the bottle was removed from the wash station. Ensure that hazardous chemicals are never stored above or near food items to protect against cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
- The hand-sink across from the dish washing station is in need of caulking. It appears that sink has pulled away from the wall, causing a gap between the wall and the sink.
- Additionally, the floor underneath the triple sink in the bar area was observed with accumulated debris (food, spilled liquids, straws, etc)

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: At least two employees were observed touching faucet handles with bare hands after the handwashing process. Discussed proper handwashing procedures with the PIC. Ensure that a barrier (paper towel) is used to operate faucet handles to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee handling phone with gloved hands and then proceeded to handle food without changing gloves. Discussed with PIC. PIC ceased activity to correct the violation. If changing activities with gloved hands, be sure to switch to a fresh set of gloves and wash hands before doing so to prevent possible contamination of food items.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The bottom inner surface of a cooler along the cook-line was observed with soiled towels and also a strong odor due to spilled liquids. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine was tested at 0ppm CL. The chlorine bucket had recently been changed during the inspection. After several cycles, the dish machine remained testing at 0ppm. An EcoLab technician was contacted to service the machine. After service, the machine was tested again at 100ppm CL. Be sure to test dish machine with CL test strips to ensure proper sanitizing concentrations.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(3) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (3) A contact time of at least 30 seconds for other chemical SANITIZING solutions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Between 5-10 fruit flies were observed near the soda gun in the bar area. PIC mentioned that a plan is in action to reduce the presence of fruit flies. EcoLab is the facility’s pest control company. A 10-day follow-up will be scheduled to ensure the reduction of fruit flies present throughout the bar area.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed a couple containers of cleaned silverware to be stored directly underneath a shelf that stores employees drinks. Discussed with an employee and the silverware was moved. Ensure that cleaned utensils are never stored underneath employees drinks and in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Overall, equipment throughout the kitchen is in need of a deep cleaning. There was a heavy accumulation of dried debris on the outside of the following areas: coolers, freezers, equipment used for cooking, hot holding equipment, etc.  When closing for the night or during slow periods, be sure to clean underneath and the sides of pieces of equipment to prevent build-up.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Overall, floors, walls, and ceilings throughout the kitchen are in need of a deep cleaning. PIC stated that a plan to thoroughly clean the kitchen will be put in place soon. Dried debris and splatter were observed on the above mentioned areas. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent build-up.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The ceiling tiles above the ice machine and also above where tortilla chips are stored (across from dish room) are in disrepair. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that ceiling tiles are always maintained in good repair. 

- There is also a broken floor tile in front of the walk in freezer. Replace floor tile.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The marinara stored in the warmer was observed at an improper hot holding temperature. The sauce was probed at 131F. PIC reheated the marinara in the microwave and the sauce was tempted again at 168F. Be sure that TCS foods are held at 135F or above to ensure proper hot holding temperatures.

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
A number of employees were observed using bare hands to turn of faucet handles after the handwashing process. Discussed with PIC to educate employees on proper hand washing procedures. Ensure that barriers are used when turning off faucet handles on a hand sink to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands.  

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
A number of utensils are being stored in a container that has crumbs at the bottom. Discussed with PIC that utensils should be rewashed and stored in a clean container. Ensure that cleaned and sanitized utensils are stored in a way that prevents them from contamination prior to use. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
A mop head was observed stored inside of the mop bucket. Discussed with PIC and mop head was removed and stored in a manner for it to air dry. Ensure that mop heads are placed in a manner that will allow them to dry properly. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The following ares are in need of sealing caulking:
-Bathroom sink in women’s restroom
-Holes in walls throughout kitchen
-Trim piece on outside corner by dish area

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
An employee’s personal drink was placed on the counter in an area where food was being prepared. Discussed with PIC and the drink was discarded. Ensure that personal items are being stored in a designated area that is separate from food items to prevent contamination. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple lids and pans along the back wall of the facility do not appear to have been completely cleaned prior to storage. Several pans in the “clean” section of the dish area are observed to also still be soiled. These items were shown to the PIC and they had them rewashed during this inspection to correct. It is also highly suggested that a conversation takes place with the dish washers in relation to ensuring that the food contact items are fully cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The two sani buckets along the prep line are observed low on the inspector’s test strips. The buckets were remade during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective concentrations at all times.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

1) Soup spoons are observed in a container with crumbs in the bottom. The location was discussed with the PIC and the spoons and cups were moved to dish for cleaning. Ensure that cleaned and sanitized utensils are stored in a way that prevents them from contamination prior to use. 2) The ice scoop used for drinks at the server station is stored between use in an ice bath that also hold containers of house made drinks and lemons. As this is a food contact surface it should not be stored in contact with ice/water that also houses potentially unclean surfaces. The scoop was washed and placed in an individual pan to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

1) Multiple shelves throughout the facility are in need of cleaning. Areas of specific note include the walk in cooler and the dish area. The locations were shown to and discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to clean often enough to prevent mold accumulation. 2) Ceiling vents in the kitchen area are in need of cleaning due to dust. These locations were shown to the PIC and they are instructed to clean often enough so as to maintain them clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

1) Seal/fill holes in the walk in cooler next to the door. These items were shown to the PIC and they are instructed to fill the holes and reseal the metal near the floor prior to the next routine inspection. 2) One of the sliding doors on the ice machine has a section that has broken off. Fill/ seal the gap so that it maintains a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

A pink hat is observed on the back post of a shelving unit that is also storing cleaned dishes in the dish area. Store employee items/clothing separate so that they do not pose a risk of contaminating food contact surfaces. The hat was removed to correct.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Several of the managers at the facility have expired Allergen Certifications. Requirement for allergen certification was discussed. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFPM with allergen certification is on-site during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not available at the handwashing sink in the back prep area or at the bar handwashing sink. Paper towels were provided during inspection. Ensure paper towels are stocked and available prior to beginning setup/prep to allow for proper handwashing between tasks/as needed.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Knives were observed in top holding compartment of prep coolers to be stored in the crevices between pans and the sides of prep coolers. One knife was observed with food debris on it and assumed to just be used for cilantro prep. Proper storage and cleaning knives between uses were discussed. All knives in question were taken to dish area for ware washing. 
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold buildup was observed around the outer surface of bar soda gun where nozzle attaches. Ensure cleaning occurs daily as needed to eliminate buildup.
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sani-bucket on cook line was observed at 0ppm quat. All other randomly checked and recently prepared sanitizer solutions were observed at 200ppm. PIC noted the solution in question may have been left from close of business the previous evening. Solution was discarded. Ensure sani-buckets are emptied at the close of business daily and that fresh sanitizer solution is provided as needed throughout daily operations. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) TCS foods in the top holding compartment of the fry line prep cooler (fry cooler) were observed with surface and internal temperatures of 55F-56F. Foods checked included sliced tomato and dressing. Top compartment is on a separate compressor and was observed off at the time of inspection. PIC turned on the top holding compartment and noted ice would be used to chill foods through lunch service until the top compartment has time to cool down and maintain temperature. Foods were placed up top within the last ~30-45 minutes and prior to placing items up top they were held in the bottom compartment of the cooler, which was holding foods below 40F. All TCS foods in the top compartment of prep cooler in question will be served or discarded by the end of lunch service.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Top holding compartment of fry cooler was off resulting in TCS foods reaching temperatures above 50F (see #22 for details). Top compartment is on a separate compressor from the bottom holding compartment of the same cooler. PIC was unsure as to how or why the top compartment was turned off but appeared to be an accidental oversight. PIC turned on the top compartment and will monitor the unit to ensure proper function.
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 DISH AREA: Floor (especially in the corner and under dish machine), floor drain, and lower portion of walls were soiled with splash/general debris.
BACK PREP AREA: Floor along walls under equipment was soiled with food/general debris.
Floor drain under prep sink was also soiled with food debris, and walls were observed with splash.
Handwashing sink was soiled with general buildup. Ponding water was also observed on the floor under the handwashing sink and may have been a result of mopping.
STORAGE: Floor and drain under ice machine were soiled with food debris.
SERVER AREA: Floor along walls under tables/behind chip warmer were soiled with food debris.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Food handler certifications for current staff were observed with expiration dates in 2021 and 2022. PIC noted facility lost track of certifications and didn’t keep up with re-certifying staff during pandemic. All staff without food manager certifications need to complete food handler training by next inspection. Ensure all staff that are not certified food managers complete an online food handler certification course within 30 days of hiring, and maintain copies of certifications on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. PIC had an allergen certification that expired as of 2021. Requirement for allergen certification was discussed. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFM with allergen certification is on-site during all hours of operation.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
A prep knife was observed sitting between containers in the prep cooler. This is not considered a clean surface or an approved storage location. Ensure knives are stored properly on a clean surface between uses. The knife was pulled for cleaning during the inspection. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The sides of the stand up freezer that holds fries and onion rings was observed soiled with encrusted grease. Additionally, the drain line for the soda gun at the bar was covered with pink/white mildew and slime. Ensure equipment is cleaned so it is clean to sight and touch.  

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The walls, pipes, and floor behind the flat top grill was observed soiled with grease and other food debris. This area and other physical facilities must be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Caulking near the dish machine sprayer and on the hand sink in the prep area is deteriorating so it is no longer smooth and easily cleanable in the gap between the wall and sink. As a result, the gap is soiled with food debris Ensure these areas are cleaned and caulking is replaced. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Drain flies were still observed in the dry storage area. Activity in the bar has decreased since the last re-inspection. Foaming cleaner is being used to clean drains. Overall, drain fly activity has decreased; however they are still present in the establishment. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed fruit/drain flies throughout the establishment. The flies were present the most in the dry storage area and bar (especially near the soda guns at the bar and sauces and soda syrup in the dry storage). They were also present around the cook line. Ensure the fruit/drain flies are eliminated from the establishment. 
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Observed employee drinks stored improperly. An open can of Red Bull was stored inside a prep cooler on the cook line. Also, an employee drink was stored on top of a prep table. Ensure employee drinks are stored in designated areas away from food and food-contact surfaces. Closed beverage containers may be stored below prep surfaces in the kitchen and food prep areas so long as they are stored below food and food contact surfaces. Drinks were moved during the inspection. 
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Observed a paper cup being used to scoop the Alfredo pesto sauce. The cup did not have a handle. Ensure a scoop with a handle is used to scoop sauce to avoid contamination with hands. The cup was replaced with a scoop that has a handle. 
3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands – except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed fruit/drain flies throughout the establishment. The flies were present the most in the dry storage area and bar. They were also present around the cook line. Ensure the fruit/drain flies are eliminated from the establishment. 
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Observed a small leak in the pipe under the the rinse sink in the dish area. A rag was wrapped around the pipe. Ensure the leak is repaired. 
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed a mop to be stored in the mop bucket. When lifted, fruit/drain flies rose from the mop head. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows them to drip dry. Mop was placed in a position that allowed it to air dry properly. 
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
3-403.11: Observed meat sauce in the steam table near the vegetable prep area to have a temperature of approximately 65F. Other foods in the steam table had a temperature of approximately 135F. Steam tables may not be used to reheat foods. Ensure rapid reheat methods are used instead. The meat sauce was rapidly reheated to 170F during the inspection. 

(A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: Observed rice and beans in the hot holding unit between the two prep coolers to be approximately 125F. TCS foods must maintain a temperature of 135 or higher. The water in the steam table was low. Water was added and the rice and bean temperature was increased. 
(A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-202.12: Observed Quaterny Ammonium and hydrogen peroxide being mixed together and used in sani buckets. Chemicals may not be mixed unless explicitly state on the manufacturer’s directions. Sani buckets were replaced with only quat solution. 
(A) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be used according to LAW(C), Manufacturer’s directions (indicate for use in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT) (P), conditions of certification (if applicable) (P), and additional conditions (if applicable) (C). (B) POISIONOUS MATERIALS shall be applied so HAZARD is not constituted to individuals and contamination from chemical is prevented (P).(C) RESTRICTED USE PESTICIDE shall be applied only by certified applicator. (Pf)

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: Observed no chlorine test strips available during the inspection. Ensure chlorine test strips are provided to check the dish machine concentration. Test strips provided during the inspection. 
A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: Observed the floor in the walk in cooler under food racks to be soiled with food debris and other debris, such as dirty dishes and old spills. Ensure the cooler floor is cleaned frequently so it is maintained clean. 
(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: Observed fruit flies in the bar and dry storage area. Flies are on sticky areas with food debris. Ensure surfaces are cleaned and flies exterminated. 
PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Observed shelves in the dry storage and the bar that are sticky with food debris. Clean these surfaces. 
NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: Observed many fruit flies throughout the establishment. Fruit flies were especially noticable in the dry storage area and the bar. Fruit flies may not be in the establishment. 
PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: 6-501.16: Observed a mop in the dry storage to be stored inside the mop bucket in an inch of old mop water. Ensure mops are stored properly after use. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: Observed an upside down sani bucket inside the bar hand sink. Ensure nothing is inside hand sinks so they can be used and accessible for hand washing. The bucket was moved during the inspection. 

(A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-101.11: Observed a gallon of chocolate milk, which was 1/4 full to have a best by date of 3/8/21. This is 3 days past the best by date. Ensure best by and expiration dates marked on packages are followed. Milk was discarded during the inspection. 
FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: 3-501.17:  Observed chocolate milk in the salad prep cooler to have no date markings. Ensure milk is properly date marked with a 7 day date marking if it is not used within 24 hours. Milk was discarded during the inspection. (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: 4-501.11: Observed the seal on the walk in freezer door to be loose and partially unattached to the door. Small amounts of ice were observed in the walk in cooler due to the improper seal. Also, the walk in freezer fan has an accumulation of ice around and the condenser and fan. Ensure the fan is working properly to avoid ice accumulation. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: 4-303.11:Observed no sanitizer (sani) buckets to be present and used during the inspection. Sani buckets are necessary to clean surfaces that are soiled or have become contaminated. Sani buckets were prepped during the inspection to correct the violation. (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 4-602.13: Observed the walk in cooler fan to be soiled with dust and other debris. This needs to be maintained clean to avoid contamination of food from dust blowing onto food surfaces. Also, carts in the kitchen and walk in cooler have accumulated food debris. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned regularly. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: Observed multiple floor areas in the facility that lacked proper cleaning. The employee seating area (the seating area near the carry out door) has spilled food and other food debris and crumbs on the floor. The floors near the wall on the walk in cooler have accumulated dirt and food debris under food racks. Ensure racks are moved to allow for proper cleaning. The floors under racks in the dry storage have accumulated debris and grease. Ensure all these areas are cleaned routinely to ensure they are clean. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

6-501.11: Observed multiple areas of disrepair in the facility. 1.) Observed multiple holes in the wall near the walk in cooler and next to the cook line hand sink. Ensure these holes are filled so they are smooth and easily cleanable. 2.) Caulking in the dish machine is worn away and moldy. Also, caulking behind the chip dispenser is cracked and not attached to the walk. Ensure the caulking is replaced and provides a proper seal to the walls. 3.) The ceiling above the stall closest to the hand sinks in the men's restroom is cracked, has a sizeable hole, and appears to have water damage. Ensure this is fixed. Also, loose debris from the ceiling could be a potential risk to patrons using the stall if loose material from the ceiling were fall. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: 6-403.11: Observed employee drinks and snacks to be in various parts of the facility. There were Swedish Fish on the chip and drink station, employee drinks and a phone on top of the dish machine, and employee drinks on top of the dish area paper towel dispenser. Ensure employees have a designated area for food and drinks to avoid potential contamination of food in the event drinks or food spill. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.
